info.title: Garmin Stats — Local Health Dashboard API
info.description:
Local-only REST API (binds 0.0.0.0) for the Holistic Runner App. Aggregates Garmin, Strava, and Withings data in a local SQLite DB.

Contract-hardening epic HRA-36 in progress: RFC 7807 `application/problem+json` error bodies with correct status codes (HRA-37 ✓), plural resource nouns incl. `/api/body-measurements` (HRA-39 ✓), the `{ data, page }` list envelope with limit/offset paging (HRA-38 ✓), PATCH (application/merge-patch+json) for partial settings updates (HRA-40 ✓), and the version prefix — every path is now under `/api/v1/...` (HRA-41 ✓) — have landed. The HRA-36 contract-hardening epic is complete. Drift between this file and the running API is treated as a bug.

runsFreeSession.name: __Host-runsfree_session
runsFreeSession.description: Validated Runs Free session; private resources derive their owner from this credential, never from client input.

from.name: from
from.description: Inclusive start date (YYYY-MM-DD). Defaults to 30 days ago.

to.name: to
to.description: Inclusive end date (YYYY-MM-DD). Defaults to today.

limit.name: limit
limit.description: Max rows to return (list envelope, HRA-38). Defaults to 50, capped at 100000.

offset.name: offset
offset.description: Rows to skip before returning (list envelope, HRA-38).

BadRequest.description: Malformed request (e.g. body is not valid JSON).

Forbidden.description: Rejected because DEMO_MODE is enabled (HRA-220) — this write is disabled for the demo.

Conflict.description: A conflicting resource already exists (e.g. duplicate name).

Unprocessable.description: Request parsed but failed a validation rule.

TooManyRequests.description: The upstream AI provider rate-limited this request.

BadGateway.description: The upstream AI provider rejected the request, was unreachable, or returned an invalid response.

ServiceUnavailable.description: The AI provider integration is not configured.

GatewayTimeout.description: The upstream AI provider request timed out.

PayloadTooLarge.description: Request body exceeds the size limit.

ServerError.description: Unexpected server error (generic; never leaks internals).

Problem.description: RFC 7807 application/problem+json error body used by every 4xx/5xx (HRA-37).

type.description: URI reference; 'about:blank' = no more info than the status.

detail.description: Human explanation specific to this occurrence.

overlaps.description: HRA-249: only on POST .../plan-instances/{id}/approve's 409 — the candidate instance and every already-approved instance whose resolved date range overlaps it.

customized_days.description: HRA-299: only on POST .../plan-instances/{id}/regenerate's 409 — every day in the requested range that already carries a customization marker and would be silently overwritten without confirm_overwrite: true.

Page.description: Pagination metadata for the list envelope (HRA-38). Offset-based.

total.description: Total rows matching the query (across all pages).

moving_time_sec.description: Active/moving time excl. pauses. Null on pre-migration rows.

descent_m.description: Always null for Strava rows (not exposed by Strava).

activity_name.description: Free-text label, e.g. a race's name.

stamina.description: Garmin Real-Time Stamina, 0-100. Null for Strava-sourced points (no source data in Strava's streams).

timezone.description: HRA-332: owner-configured IANA timezone. NULL means not yet configured — the default new plan instances fall back to when creation supplies no explicit/browser-fallback value.

accent_color.description: Paired 1:1 with palette (sky=metal, amber=warm, graphite=graphite) — no longer independently settable, see the /palette endpoint.

palette.description: Dashboard palette flavor. 'metal'/'warm' cross with theme (dark/light) for 4 total looks; 'graphite' is a third, standalone, dark-only palette (no light counterpart). 'auto' is the DEFAULT sentinel for 'never explicitly chosen' (same relationship 'auto' has with theme) — the client resolves it to 'graphite' when the resolved theme is dark, 'warm' when light; never accepted by PUT /palette. Replaces the earlier style_pack (HRA-119).

demo_mode.description: Computed from the DEMO_MODE env var (HRA-220), not a stored column — read-only, never accepted by any settings write. true means the write endpoints listed in that Story's Forbidden response are rejected server-side; the frontend uses this to disable the matching controls.

DateRangeEntry.description: A saved named date range, optionally linked to the race it led up to.

FeedbackEntry.description: An anonymous visitor feedback submission (HRA-226) — every field is independently optional; the request is rejected 422 if every field is empty/absent.

pricing_why_not_free_text.description: Only meaningful (not required) when pricing_choice is free_only.

RaceActivity.description: A race-type activity, as offered by the 'link a race' dropdown.

PlanTemplate.description: A reusable RunPlan DSL v1 template (HRA-111/HRA-112, amended HRA-113) — parsed but pace-unresolved; see docs/runplan-dsl.md.

approved_at.description: HRA-113 gate 2: NULL = not approved. Set via POST .../approve; cleared by any subsequent PUT.

ResolvedSegment.description: One resolved workout segment (continuous/interval/progression/rest_block) — same shape as domain/runplan's WorkoutSegment, with intensities replaced by resolved *_sec_per_km pace numbers.

PlanInstanceDay.description: One resolved day of a plan instance.

scheduled_time.description: HRA-149: HH:MM, nullable — NULL reads as the 08:00 default at display time, never backfilled.

customized_at.description: HRA-299: nullable timestamp — non-null means this day's workout content was individually edited (PATCH .../days/{dayId}'s dsl branch) or swapped after creation. Always NULL on a freshly created/regenerated row.

PlanInstanceDayEdit.description: One day submitted to PATCH /api/v1/plan-instances/{id} (HRA-115, method changed from PUT to PATCH in HRA-135) — raw DSL text plus the section/week/date scope it lives in, not pre-resolved segments. The backend re-parses dsl against that scope's own effective pace policy (template Section/Week PacePolicy merged with the instance's pace_overrides) and resolves it the same way instantiation resolves a segment.

dsl.description: Raw D-line text, same grammar as a template, e.g. "D3 [interval]: 4x3000m @ RG-20 r:1km @ RG+10".

PlanInstanceDayWithInstance.description: A PlanInstanceDay denormalized with its owning instance's own name (HRA-206) — GET /api/v1/plan-instance-days's response shape, so a same-day picker across multiple instances can label each option without a second lookup per row.

instance_name.description: The owning plan_instances.name — nullable only for the same legacy-migration reason PlanInstance.name is (HRA-114).

AssociationView.description: HRA-334: one activity's link to a planned workout (plan_instance_days.workout_id), denormalized with its CURRENT plan-day context. workout_id/status and every plan-day field are null when no association exists yet (extra/unplanned — a legitimate state, not an error) or once the linked workout has left Current entirely.

PlanInstance.description: One resolved instantiation of a plan template for a specific race.

pace_overrides.description: JSON-serialized PacePolicy overrides applied at instantiation.

approved_at.description: HRA-113 gate 2: NULL = not approved. Set via POST .../approve; cleared by any subsequent PATCH that applies a field (HRA-135, was PUT).

name.description: HRA-114: the instance's own name, distinct from its source template's. Required on create; nullable at the DB level only for pre-HRA-114 rows (migration-backfilled).

event.description: HRA-114: denormalized copy of the template's event at instantiation time. Never independently settable.

race_name.description: HRA-121: free-text description of the race this instance targets. Independent of target_activity_id.

race_date.description: HRA-121: free-text race date, independent of target_activity_id.

race_url.description: HRA-121: free-text race link (e.g. a registration page), not validated as a well-formed URL. Independent of target_activity_id.

schedule_timezone.description: HRA-332: IANA timezone governing plan-date interpretation, activity local-date conversion, report asOf boundaries, and missed-workout eligibility. Correctable via PATCH until the Original baseline freezes, then rejected with 409.

original_start_date.description: HRA-332: the Original baseline's start_date — mirrors Current until frozen, then untouched forever.

original_days_snapshot.description: HRA-332: JSON-serialized Original baseline day snapshot (same per-day shape as PlanInstanceDay, without id/instance_id) — mirrors Current until frozen, then untouched forever.

current_revision.description: HRA-336: monotonic, bumped exactly once per successful semantic mutation of Current (edits, moves, swaps, additions, removals, start-date changes, regeneration). Starts at 1.

original_revision.description: HRA-336: follows current_revision while Original still mirrors Current (pre-freeze); stops changing forever once the Original baseline freezes. Starts at 1.

WorkoutDatasetMetrics.description: One dataset's totals for a single workout (HRA-336) — an isolated Original/Current/Actual measurement, never averaged across activities.

approximate.description: true if the distance was itself derived from a duration->distance conversion.

paceSecPerKm.description: distance-total / time-total; null when nothing resolves, never 0.

WorkoutActualEvidence.description: One accepted activity's evidence for this workout (HRA-334 status + HRA-335's elapsed/active/paused split).

WorkoutHrEvidence.description: Actual-only HR evidence (HRA-337) — duration-weighted average across every accepted activity, never a planned value.

WorkoutStaminaEvidence.description: The ONE recorded stamina series (HRA-337, from the first accepted activity's track_points.stamina) — firstValid is never assumed to be 100%.

WorkoutPauseDetail.description: One detected pause (HRA-337) — same fields the existing frontend PauseInspectionDialog already renders for an activity viewed directly.

provenance.description: 'recorded' = a real device recording gap; 'inferred' = the near-zero-speed heuristic.

WorkoutPauseEvidence.description: Pause evidence for this workout's accepted activities (HRA-337) — reuses domain/workout-metrics.ts's canonical detectPauseEvents, never a second detection algorithm.

hasTrackData.description: false when no track_points existed to run detection over at all — distinct from a real zero-pauses result.

WorkoutReport.description: Response of GET .../plan-instances/{id}/reports/workouts/{workoutId} (HRA-336; hr/stamina/pauses added HRA-337).

originalEqualsCurrent.description: true only for lineage 'unchanged' — the UI collapses to one Planned column in this case.

hasAmbiguousEvidence.description: true when at least one 'unresolved' association exists for this workout — visible, never trusted (AC11).

race.description: isRace=false for a non-race workout. When true: target* comes from the planned segments (Current, falling back to Original), actual comparison is always elapsed time (never moving/active) — no official-result data source exists yet, so actualSource is always 'activity' or 'none'.

hr.description: null when there is no accepted evidence activity (HRA-337).

stamina.description: null when there is no accepted evidence activity, or track_points weren't loaded for it (HRA-337).

pauses.description: null when there is no accepted evidence activity, or track_points weren't loaded for it (HRA-337).

structuredQualityEvidence.description: HRA-342 slot — always {available: false, reason: 'not_implemented'} today.

ReportResult.description: Response of HRA-335's shared buildReport engine (domain/reporting/report.ts) — the ONE calculation every report scope (week, entire-plan, and future HRA-341 scopes) shares. Never returned bare at the HTTP level; always nested inside WeekReport.report or PlanReport.overall/weeks[].report.

datasets.description: Each dataset's fields are present only for the requested metrics — an unrequested field is absent, never a present zero.

comparisons.description: adaptation (Original-vs-Current), execution (Current-vs-Actual), outcome (Original-vs-Actual) — each independently selectable, never substituting for one another.

structuredQualityEvidence.description: HRA-342 slot — always {available: false, reason: 'not_implemented'} today.

WorkoutIdentity.description: Labels a workout_id (report.ts's engine returns only ids) for display — mirrors WorkoutReport.identity's own shape.

AggregateEvidence.description: HR/stamina/pause evidence at week/plan (multi-workout) scope (HRA-338, extending HRA-337's rules). HR and pauses are safe to blend across every accepted activity in scope; stamina deliberately is NOT (comparableStamina) — a depletion curve from a short easy day and a long run aren't comparable quantities, so at most ONE session's own stamina series is surfaced, never a blended average.

hr.description: null only when there are no accepted activities in scope at all.

comparableStamina.description: null when nothing in scope qualifies (no race, and no unique strict-max-distance completed run — a tie never guesses).

WeekReport.description: Response of GET .../plan-instances/{id}/reports/weeks (HRA-338). A 'week' is a planned workout's own structural slot (section_name + week_number, lineage.ts's own definition), never a calendar-date span.

workouts.description: One entry per workout with either side inside this week (a moved_in/moved_out workout still appears).

structuredQualityEvidence.description: HRA-342 slot — always {available: false, reason: 'not_implemented'} today.

PlanReport.description: Response of GET .../plan-instances/{id}/reports/plan (HRA-338) — the whole plan's own isolated totals plus a per-week breakdown for progression.

weeks.description: Ordered chronologically by each week's own earliest known date, never lexicographically.

structuredQualityEvidence.description: HRA-342 slot — always {available: false, reason: 'not_implemented'} today.

RangeReport.description: Response of GET /api/v1/reports/range (HRA-341) — the date-range/race-range report. Unlike WeekReport/PlanReport (one plan instance), this scans EVERY plan instance whose Original or Current span overlaps [from,to] and gives each its own isolated ReportResult — an instance's own evidence never leaks into another instance's report within the same window. `aggregate` sums across every included instance (Actual is computed range-wide, directly from every accepted activity in the window, never as a sum of possibly-partial per-instance actuals). `unplanned`/`ambiguous` are range-wide (never duplicated per instance).

grouping.description: Automatic presentation grouping by window length (AC: workout for short ranges, week for medium, month only for long ranges) — reuses Overview & Trends' own preset ladder, an advisory hint the caller applies to how it groups the per-instance execution/outcome entries it already has, not a second server-side bucketing.

instances.description: One entry per plan instance overlapping [from,to]. Empty is a truthful 'no-plan' state, never an error.

dateSpan.description: This instance's own span, intersected with [from,to].

unplanned.description: Range-wide extra/unplanned activities, included by their own actual local date, Actual-only.

ambiguous.description: Range-wide unresolved associations — visible in coverage, never in a trusted total.

qualityEvidence.description: HRA-341's own structured quality-workout range rollup, reusing HRA-342's per-workout structured comparison — CURRENT run-type days only, classified as repetition/threshold/tempo/progressive.

workouts.description: Range drill-down: the exact quality workouts, each with its full per-repetition/block/phase structure and alignment provenance (StructuredQualityComparison).

comparison.description: StructuredQualityComparison — same shape WorkoutReport.structuredQualityEvidence carries when available (kind/available/segments/totals/wholeSessionPaceSecPerKm).

ParseWarning.description: A non-fatal parse issue (HRA-113: nothing the parser encounters is a hard error — everything degrades to a warning). Day-scoped warnings live on the day itself; this shape is also used for the plan-scoped list (unrecognized lines, circular pace refs).

GeneratedPlan.description: Response of POST /api/v1/plan-templates/generate — a parse-only preview, never persisted.

plan.description: The parsed RunPlan (domain/runplan/types.ts), with per-day warnings on each DayEntry.

warnings.description: Plan-scoped warnings only (day-scoped warnings live on each DayEntry inside plan).

SourceExtractionResult.description: Response of POST /api/v1/source-files/extract — never persisted; nothing is written to disk.

sourceText.description: Extracted text, line-endings normalized to \n. Never empty (an empty extraction is rejected, 422).

sourceType.description: The REAL sniffed content type (from the file's own bytes), which may differ from the sourceType the caller declared.

pageCount.description: Present only when sourceType is pdf.

post.summary: Submit anonymous visitor feedback (HRA-226)
post.description: free_text, pricing_choice, pricing_why_not_free_text, feature_interest, feature_interest_other_free_text, and app_type_choice are all independently optional, but the request is rejected 422 if every field is empty/absent. pricing_choice, when present, must be one of the four defined tiers. feature_interest, when present, is an array whose entries are each multi_user_coach, shared_groups, or curated_content_feed. app_type_choice, when present, must be cloud or desktop. Deliberately NOT gated by DEMO_MODE — the one write route the demo guard must not block, since demo visitors are a primary source of submissions.

get.summary: The fixed Training/Race lookup

post.summary: Parse-only preview of DSL source — never persists (HRA-113)
post.description: Runs the same parse as POST /api/v1/plan-templates without writing a row. 422 only if the DSL fails to parse outright (ParseResult.ok:false); a plan with day-level warnings still returns 200 — what a review UI calls on every edit before the user is ready to save.

post.summary: Parse-only-style preview of the AI conversion prompt (HRA-326) — never persists
post.description: Composes the same 'Plan text -> RunPlan DSL' conversion prompt via composeConversionPrompt() (domain/runplan/prompt-composer.ts) that a future real AI provider call will use — one function, not two implementations, so preview and the real send can never drift. text is required; language/event/event_name/distance_m/unit are all optional context fields. Plan text containing tag-like substrings (e.g. </training_plan>, <system>) is escaped so it can't terminate the envelope early or be read as new instructions.

post.summary: Generate RunPlan DSL from plan text via the configured AI provider (HRA-329) — real, billable call
post.description: Composes the identical conversion prompt as prompt-preview (composeConversionPrompt(), never a second copy) and sends it to the configured provider (garmin-stats/src/integrations/plan-template-ai.ts, HRA-325). Never persists — the caller drops the returned dsl into the existing Workout DSL editor, which re-parses/validates it exactly like a manual paste; the result is never auto-saved or auto-activated. Demo-guarded (403 when DEMO_MODE is on) since every call has a real external cost. Provider failures surface as an honest status instead of a generic 500: 503 (not configured), 502 (auth/network/http-error/empty or malformed response), 429 (rate-limited), 504 (timeout).

get.summary: List plan templates, newest first

post.summary: Save a template, parsing and validating its DSL source
post.description: Rejects (422) unless the DSL parses and has zero outstanding warnings anywhere in the tree (HRA-113 — replaces HRA-111's bottom-up valid/errors model; nothing the parser encounters is a hard error anymore, e.g. an interval missing rest is now a warning, not a rejection). event is required, one of 5k|10k|half|marathon|custom; distance_m is required iff event is custom, rejected (422) for any other event (HRA-120 — event/distance_m are explicit request fields now, overwriting whatever the DSL's now-vestigial EVENT/DISTANCE lines produced). The 422 body's errors[] lists every flagged day.

distance_m.description: Required iff event is custom; rejected for any other event.

get.summary: Get one plan template

put.summary: Replace a plan template (re-parses dsl_source from scratch)
put.description: Same zero-warning gate as POST, same event/distance_m validation (HRA-120). Always clears approved_at back to NULL (HRA-113 gate 2 — any edit revokes approval, even one that still parses with zero warnings).

distance_m.description: Required iff event is custom; rejected for any other event.

delete.summary: Delete a plan template (ON DELETE CASCADE removes every derived instance, no trash)

post.summary: Approve a template (gate 2, HRA-113)
post.description: Sets approved_at. Only meaningful on an already-saved (zero-warning) template — approval is a deliberate human sign-off on the exact currently-saved state, revoked by any subsequent PUT.

get.summary: Structural check: can this template use mobile simplified race-plan creation? (HRA-302)
get.description: Read-only, never persists. Reuses instantiatePlan/pace.ts's own resolver (domain/runplan/mobile-eligibility.ts) rather than re-deriving anchor/offset logic: eligible when the template's own pace policy leaves at most one anchor symbolic and supplying any value for it makes every day resolve with needs_review false. race_pace_anchor is that single anchor name, or null when either no anchor is needed (already fully resolvable) or the template is not eligible. reason is one of already-resolved, ambiguous-anchors, unresolvable, or null when eligible with an anchor.

post.summary: Parse-only preview of an instantiation, never persists (HRA-302)
post.description: Mirrors POST .../instantiate's goal_time -> pace_overrides conversion and instantiatePlan resolution, but never writes a plan_instances row. Feeds the mobile simplified-creation review step: shows the derived start_date and every resolved plan-level anchor pace before the runner commits to the real Create action. needs_review is true if any resolved day still needs review (e.g. an unsupported anchor, or the template turns out not to be fully resolvable) — the caller must not proceed to the real instantiate call when true.

goal_time.description: HH:MM:SS — alternate input for race_pace_anchor's value, converted via distance.

race_pace_anchor.description: Which anchor goal_time resolves to. Required whenever goal_time is supplied.

post.summary: Resolve a template for one race: override pace anchors + a start date, persist the result
post.description: name (HRA-114) is required — the instance's own name; the created instance's event is never a request parameter, always auto-populated from the template. target_activity_id (if given) is validated like date_ranges.activity_id, but against the resolved plan's last day — checked fully before any write, so a rejected request leaves no orphaned rows. goal_time (HRA-113) is an alternate way to supply a pace anchor's value — race_pace_anchor names which one, and is required whenever goal_time is supplied (HRA-121, no default; earlier versions hardcoded RG) — converted via distance (distance_m if given, else the template's own distance_m, else the event's standard distance; a custom event's distance_m is mandatory at template save time, HRA-120, so this call's own distance_m only overrides it, never supplies a missing one). Supplying both goal_time and an explicit pace_overrides value for the same race_pace_anchor is rejected as ambiguous. race_name/race_date (HRA-121, both optional) describe the race this instance targets, independent of target_activity_id.

pace_overrides.description: anchor -> pace value string, same grammar as a PACE line's right-hand side, e.g. {"RG": "6:40/mi"}.

goal_time.description: HH:MM:SS — alternate input for the race_pace_anchor's value, converted via distance.

race_pace_anchor.description: Which anchor goal_time resolves to. Required whenever goal_time is supplied — no default (HRA-121).

distance_m.description: Optional override of the distance used to convert goal_time — the template's own distance_m (mandatory for a custom-event template) is used when this is omitted.

race_name.description: Free-text race description (HRA-121), independent of target_activity_id.

race_date.description: Free-text race date (HRA-121), independent of target_activity_id.

race_url.description: Free-text race link, e.g. a registration page (HRA-121), independent of target_activity_id. Not validated as a well-formed URL.

rest_day_label.description: Free-text label (HRA-124) attached as `notes` on every day auto-filled to plug a gap in a template week (a D-number 1-7 the template never declared for that week).

schedule_timezone.description: HRA-332: explicit IANA schedule timezone for this instance. Omitted, defaults to settings.timezone, then browser_timezone_fallback, then the literal 'UTC'.

browser_timezone_fallback.description: HRA-332: creation-time-only fallback used when schedule_timezone is omitted and settings.timezone is unconfigured.

201.description: The created instance, with its resolved days.

get.summary: List plan instances, newest first (HRA-118)
get.description: template_id is optional — omit for all instances, or scope to one template's own instances. 404 if template_id doesn't reference a real template.

get.summary: Get the one approved plan instance whose resolved days cover a date (HRA-248)
get.description: Feeds "Your agenda"'s today-centered home view. Extends the daysByDateAndWorkoutType pattern, scoped to approved_at IS NOT NULL and with no workout_type filter (a REST day is a real dated row too, HRA-124, and must resolve just as well as a workout day). 404 (not an empty 200) when no approved instance's resolved days include the date — lets the frontend tell "no active plan today" apart from a genuine fetch failure. Newest-instance-first if more than one approved instance's days cover the same date (overlap detection/activation blocking is a sibling Story, out of scope here).

200.description: The active instance, with its resolved days.

get.summary: Every run-type plan_instance_day matching a calendar date, across every instance (HRA-206)
get.description: Feeds ActivityDetailBody's same-day planned-vs-actual picker: 0 matches -> no UI change, 1 -> the chart renders automatically, >=2 -> a picker labeled by instance name. Only workout_type === 'run' ever matches (REST/CROSS/STRENGTH/OTHER are excluded, docs/runplan-dsl.md). Matches across every instance regardless of approved_at state. No pagination envelope — a plain (possibly empty) array.

get.summary: Get one resolved plan instance, with its days

patch.summary: Partially update an instance's name/race info/resolved days (HRA-135, replacing the earlier PUT)
patch.description: All body fields are optional, but at least one is required (422 otherwise). Each provided field replaces its current value; every omitted field is left untouched. race_name/race_date/race_url are nullable — send null to explicitly clear one. `days`, when provided, still fully replaces the day set (unchanged semantics from the old PUT, HRA-113/HRA-114/HRA-115) — each day is raw DSL text plus its section/week/date scope; the backend looks up that day's section/week in the source template's own parsed plan for its effective PacePolicy, merges in the instance's own pace_overrides, re-parses dsl against that policy, and resolves it the same way instantiation resolves a segment. Rejects (422) if any day's fresh parse still needs review, listing every flagged day. event is never accepted here, read-only/derived from the template. Never touches or re-instantiates the source template; an instance may diverge from what the template would currently produce. Clears approved_at back to NULL whenever any field in the body is applied, same gate-2 rule as the template PUT. schedule_timezone (HRA-332) corrects the instance's IANA timezone — rejected with 409 once the Original baseline has frozen. Whenever days and/or schedule_timezone are applied before Original freezes, Original is re-mirrored to match.

200.description: The updated instance, with its resolved days.

delete.summary: Delete a plan instance (ON DELETE CASCADE removes its days, no trash, HRA-115)

get.summary: The single-workout/race report for one planned workout (HRA-336)
get.description: Reads Original, Current, their revisions, accepted HRA-334 association evidence, and asOf from one consistent application-level read boundary (services/reporting.service.ts) — the result never mixes plan content from one revision with a different reported revision. Reuses HRA-333's lineage classifier and HRA-335's shared metrics primitives rather than a second calculation engine. A workout counts as the plan's race day when its own placement date equals the instance's race_date (HRA-121); race actual comparison always uses elapsed time, never moving/active time. No official-result data source exists yet — race.actualSource is always 'activity' or 'none'.

parameters.name: workoutId
parameters.description: The stable HRA-333 workout_id (not a plan_instance_days row id).

parameters.name: as_of
parameters.description: Explicit ISO instant for the report's future/missed cutoff; defaults to the server's current time.

get.summary: The week report for one planned week — group-by-workout adaptation/execution/outcome (HRA-338)
get.description: Reuses HRA-335's shared buildReport engine (domain/reporting/report.ts), scoped to ONE week: a planned workout's own structural slot (section_name + week_number, lineage.ts's own 'moved' definition), never a calendar-date span. A workout that moved into or out of this exact slot still surfaces as moved_in/moved_out rather than silently vanishing from one side. evidence.hr/pauses blend across every accepted activity in this week's own date span; evidence.comparableStamina never blends — at most one session (the week's race, else its strict-max-distance completed run) carries its own stamina series.

parameters.name: section_name
parameters.description: The week's own section_name, as returned on any plan_instance_days row for it.

parameters.name: week_number
parameters.description: The week's own week_number within that section.

parameters.name: range
parameters.description: plan_to_date (default) excludes future workouts from execution/outcome entirely; full_plan keeps them as upcoming context.

parameters.name: as_of
parameters.description: Explicit ISO instant for the report's future/missed cutoff; defaults to the server's current time.

get.summary: The entire-plan report — grouped by week for progression, drilling down to workouts (HRA-338)
get.description: Reuses HRA-335's shared buildReport engine once for the whole plan's own isolated totals (overall) and once per week (weeks[], in chronological order) — never a second calculation engine. An empty plan (no days on either side yet) returns an empty report rather than 404ing (the instance itself still exists).

parameters.name: range
parameters.description: plan_to_date (default) excludes future workouts from execution/outcome entirely; full_plan keeps them as upcoming context. Applies identically to `overall` and every entry in `weeks`.

parameters.name: as_of
parameters.description: Explicit ISO instant for the report's future/missed cutoff; defaults to the server's current time.

get.summary: The date-range/race-range report — cross-plan, grouped automatically by window length (HRA-341)
get.description: Unlike every other report above (scoped to one plan instance), this scans EVERY plan instance whose Original or Current span overlaps [from,to] and gives each its own isolated buildReport call (associations pre-filtered to that instance's own workout ids, so one instance's evidence never leaks into another's totals within the same window). aggregate sums across every included instance; its Actual dataset and the range-wide unplanned/ambiguous lists are computed once against every activity in the window, never per instance. A race-range is just a saved date_ranges row's own {from,to} resolved by the caller before this call — there is no separate race-range endpoint. An empty window (no instances, no activities) returns an explicit empty report rather than 404ing.

parameters.name: range
parameters.description: plan_to_date (default) excludes future workouts from execution/outcome entirely; full_plan keeps them as upcoming context. Applies identically to every included instance.

parameters.name: as_of
parameters.description: Explicit ISO instant for the report's future/missed cutoff; defaults to the server's current time.

patch.summary: Partially update a single resolved day (HRA-149)
patch.description: A smaller, more honest write than PATCH .../plan-instances/{id}'s bulk days replace: one field's worth of edit on one already-existing day. Body is {dsl?, notes?, scheduled_time?}, all optional but at least one required (422 otherwise), each validated independently. dsl, when supplied, is re-parsed against this day's own existing section/week/date scope and the template's effective PacePolicy (merged with the instance's pace_overrides) and resolved the same way the bulk days-replace path does; rejected (422) if the fresh parse still needs review. notes overrides whatever the dsl parse itself produced for that field, when both are supplied together. scheduled_time must be HH:MM 24-hour, or null to clear back to the 08:00 display default. HRA-249: no longer rejected once the instance is approved — HRA-126's lock is a frontend-only warning now; only activating a conflicting instance is hard-blocked (see .../approve). Never touches or re-instantiates the source template.

dsl.description: Raw D-line text, same grammar as a template, e.g. "D3 [interval]: 4x3000m @ RG-20 r:1km @ RG+10".

scheduled_time.description: HH:MM, 24-hour. null clears back to the 08:00 display default.

post.summary: Parse-only preview of a day's DSL edit, never persists (HRA-162)
post.description: What the List view's per-day editor calls (debounced) as the user types, so warning feedback updates live instead of only after the whole-day bulk Save round-trip. Reuses the exact same parseDayEntry call and ParseWarning taxonomy the persisting PATCH .../days/{dayId} validates against, against this day's own existing section/week scope and the template's effective PacePolicy (merged with the instance's pace_overrides) — never a separate client-side grammar reimplementation. Always 200: parseDayEntry itself never hard-rejects (docs/runplan-dsl.md's warnings-only model), it only ever produces warnings. No approved-instance guard, unlike the PATCH above: this never mutates anything.

dsl.description: Raw D-line text, same grammar as a template, e.g. "D3 [interval]: 4x3000m @ RG-20 r:1km @ RG+10".

200.description: The fresh parse of this DSL text — when the parse itself succeeds, also the resolved day (workout_type/segments/activity_target/activity_description), so the caller can compute this day's own distance client-side without persisting; omitted when the parse fails and needs_review is true.

get.summary: Export one resolved day as a Garmin Workout .fit file (HRA-202)
get.description: Wraps toGarminWorkoutFit (integrations/garmin-workout.ts) for one plan_instance_days row. Read-only: nothing is parsed or persisted, so an approved instance is not guarded against. Rejected (422) exactly when toGarminWorkoutFit itself rejects the day — needs_review, or a workout_type other than run/rest.

200.description: Binary FIT file. Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="<instance name>_<YYYYMMDD>.fit".

get.summary: Export every exportable day in a section (or one week within it) as a Garmin Workout .fit zip (HRA-203)
get.description: Bundles one .fit per exportable plan_instance_days row in scope (filtered by section_name, and optionally week_number) into a single uncompressed (STORE) zip, reusing the same toGarminWorkoutFit path as the day-level export above. A day toGarminWorkoutFit itself rejects (needs_review, or a workout_type other than run/rest) is skipped rather than failing the request — X-Export-Total/X-Export-Included/X-Export-Skipped response headers report the counts, since the body itself is opaque binary. 422 with no zip written when zero days in scope are exportable.

parameters.name: section_name
parameters.description: The plan_instance_days.section_name to scope the export to.

parameters.name: week_number
parameters.description: When given, narrows the export to this week within section_name; omitted exports the whole section.

200.description: Binary zip file. Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="<instance name>_<first date:yyyymmdd>-<last date:yyyymmdd>.zip". Also carries X-Export-Total/X-Export-Included/X-Export-Skipped headers.

post.summary: Approve a plan instance (gate 2, HRA-113; overlap-blocked HRA-249)
post.description: Same gate-2 semantics as the template approve endpoint. HRA-249: before approving, the candidate's resolved date range (MIN/MAX over its plan_instance_days) is compared inclusively and date-only against every OTHER already-approved instance's own range. Any overlap (start/end boundary, full containment either direction, or a shared boundary date) 409s and never sets approved_at — the Problem body's `overlaps` field names the candidate and every conflicting instance, each with its own range and the overlap period. No override exists.

post.summary: Regenerate an instance's days from a cutover date onward (HRA-132)
post.description: effective_from is required and server-floored to today — never trusted from the client. Days with date < effective_from are never modified or deleted. Days with date >= effective_from are fully regenerated from the template's own DSL (via instantiatePlan, not from the instance's already-resolved days — those already discarded each day's original symbolic pace anchor) using start_date/pace_overrides, falling back to the instance's own current value for whichever is omitted. pace_overrides, when supplied, is the instance's new COMPLETE override map (same semantics as /instantiate's own field), not a partial merge on top of what was stored before. Existing manual edits on days >= effective_from are discarded (documented behavior, not a bug). Clears approved_at, same gate-2 rule as the instance PUT. HRA-299: before mutating, a preflight checks every currently-persisted day in [effective_from, end] for a customization marker (set by PATCH .../days/{dayId}'s dsl branch, or a swap) — if any are found and confirm_overwrite isn't true, 409s naming every affected day instead of silently discarding them; retry with confirm_overwrite: true to proceed.

start_date.description: Optional — defaults to the instance's own current start_date.

pace_overrides.description: Optional — the instance's new COMPLETE override map, anchor -> pace value string. Defaults to the instance's own currently-stored overrides when omitted.

effective_from.description: The cutover date. Must not be before today (422 otherwise, enforced server-side).

confirm_overwrite.description: HRA-299: required (true) to proceed once the preflight finds any customized day in range. Ignored/unnecessary when none are found.

200.description: The updated instance, with its regenerated days.

post.summary: Atomically exchange the logical workouts occupying two calendar slots (HRA-333 follow-up)
post.description: Replaces the old two-call PATCH .../days/{dayId} swap flow — each of those calls was its own transaction, so plan_instance_days' deferred (instance_id, workout_id) unique constraint could never actually resolve at commit. This endpoint locks both day rows, verifies both exist and belong to the requested instance, and exchanges their workout_id in one statement within one transaction; the deferred constraint is only needed to let each row's new value pass Postgres' per-row uniqueness check mid-statement. Neither slot's own id/date/scheduled_time moves, and plan_instance_workouts (content, customization) and workout_associations (both keyed by (instance_id, workout_id)) are never written — both stay attached to the logical workout, not the slot. 404 if either day_a_id/day_b_id doesn't exist or belongs to a different instance; the whole transaction rolls back in that case, so a partially-invalid request never partially applies.

day_b_id.description: plan_instance_days.id of the second slot. Must differ from day_a_id.

get.summary: Translation bundle for a language

post.summary: Extract plan text from an uploaded .txt/.csv/.pdf file (HRA-327)
post.description: Decodes contentBase64 and sniffs the REAL content type from the bytes (a PDF signature within the leading 1024 bytes), never trusting sourceType or the filename extension alone — a file declared pdf that isn't one is rejected as corrupt/misnamed rather than silently read as text, and a genuine PDF is extracted as one even if declared txt/csv. .txt/.csv content is decoded as UTF-8 and returned unchanged apart from line-ending normalization. .pdf content is parsed via unpdf (pure-JS, no native deps); an encrypted PDF, a corrupt/non-PDF file, an oversized file (>10MB) or overlong PDF (>200 pages), and an image-only/no-extractable-text PDF each 422/413 with a distinct, actionable detail message — none return 200 with empty/garbage sourceText. Nothing is ever written to disk; nothing persists across the request.

sourceType.description: Caller's declared type (e.g. from the file extension) — verified, not trusted, against the actual bytes.
